error: A label or trigger (regions, the election, states' rights) replaces slavery as the cause
shows: A label or trigger replaces the underlying conflict
source: Secession declarations; anticipated error from memory
example: The war came because Lincoln won, beside: the election triggered secession by leaders defending slavery
if_many: Reread one declaration's first paragraph together; sort trigger from cause

error: Every Northerner opposed slavery and every Southerner supported secession
shows: Regions replace varied people, interests and dissent
source: Region model; anticipated error from memory
example: The South wanted to leave, beside: secession conventions in states where many residents, enslaved people among them, had no vote
if_many: Map dissent: free Black Northerners, Unionist counties, enslaved people

error: Lincoln freed everyone immediately; military victory alone explains emancipation
shows: Policy limits, change and Black agency disappear
source: Emancipation Proclamation; anticipated error from memory
example: Lincoln freed all slaves in 1863, beside: the Proclamation covered areas in rebellion and needed armies and people escaping to make it real
if_many: Shade the Proclamation's areas on a map; leave the loyal slave states, Tennessee and the excepted parishes and counties unshaded, Fortress Monroe (Elizabeth City County) among them, and mark where people fled

error: Lee was Confederate president; Gettysburg ended the war; battles were interchangeable
shows: Political and military roles, chronology and geography are confused
source: Progression row us1-civil-war; anticipated error from memory
example: Gettysburg won the war, beside: Gettysburg turned back an invasion in 1863 and the war went on until 1865
if_many: Sort the three leaders by office; put the three battles on one timeline

error: Only generals and male combatants served; photographs prove everyone's motives
shows: Service and source limits are narrowed or erased
source: Douglass, Tubman and Rice; anticipated error from memory
example: The photograph shows they wanted to fight, beside: a posed company photograph shows uniforms and arms, not feelings
if_many: Sort what a photograph shows from what it cannot; add a woman's service

error: The amendments meant the same thing or guaranteed equal access at once
shows: Distinct legal changes and enforcement are collapsed
source: Amendment transcripts; anticipated error from memory
example: The 14th gave Black men the vote, beside: the 15th barred racial exclusion from voting; the 14th made citizenship and equal protection
if_many: Three-column sort of amendment, change and enforcement

error: Reconstruction achieved nothing, ended naturally, or lost all constitutional gains in 1877
shows: Black institution-building, organized terror, policy choices and lasting law are hidden
source: Reconstruction progression; community report and Hayes library; anticipated error from memory
example: Reconstruction just ended in 1877, beside: violence and a federal retreat overthrew governments while the amendments stayed law
if_many: Line up what survived and what was overthrown, with who acted

error: An old account is true, a biased account useless, or disagreement can be ignored
shows: Evidence is cut off from who made it, its setting and the claim's limits
source: Published inquiry indicators; anticipated error from memory
example: Both views deserve equal standing, beside: the postwar claim fails against the 1861 record
if_many: Model one source test again, then pairs test a second claim

error: Adding quotations or correcting spelling counts as revising historical reasoning
shows: Claims and counterclaims have not changed in response to evidence
source: Published inquiry indicators; anticipated error from memory
example: Draft 2 adds two quotations, beside: draft 2 narrows the claim to leaders and answers the election counterclaim

error: The Union's war aims never changed: it fought to end slavery from the first day, or never did
shows: The change from restoring the Union to emancipation, and who pushed it, disappears

example: The Union fought to free the slaves from 1861, beside: in 1861 the aim was the Union; by 1863 freedom in areas in rebellion was a war aim
if_many: Put Sources A and C side by side with their dates; students say what changed and who pushed

error: Western land was empty when the government gave it away

source: Pacific Railway Act section 2; expert day 79
